episodes.200106: A backdoor front pushed through northeast NM during the morning hours of April 25th stalling across east central NM midday. Additionally, a dryline backed west into the southeast plains of New Mexico. These surface boundaries allowed higher low level Gulf moisture. Daytime heating, combined with the higher moisture, lift from the aforementioned boundaries and an upper level shortwave overhead and stronger vertical wind shear, resulted in the development of discrete severe storms across far east central NM. These storms produced large hail up to 2.75 inches in diameter. Training thunderstorms between Tucumcari and Clovis resulted in some flash flooding on State Highway 275. Upslope easterly behind and north of the backdoor front resulted in the development of additional strong to severe storms across the northeast and east central plains during the overnight hours of April 25th into April 26th. Some of the storms resulted in quarter size hail and flash flooding in Fort Sumner. Rainfall amounts of around 4 inches were observed in town. Storms exited into West Texas around sunrise April 26th. Another round of discrete supercells developed along and east of a stalled surface front across the eastern highlands and plains and ahead of an upper low moving into California. These supercells brought large hail as well as producing brief tornadoes south of Fort Sumner and north and northeast of Roswell. Storms dissipated during the late evening hours with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.200119: A weak cold front interacting with a sea breeze circulation within a modestly unstable and sheared environment, led to a thunderstorm capable of producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.200553: A thunderstorm briefly became severe producing 1.5 inch hail along US 287 between Hugo and Boyero.
episodes.200641: Although large scale lift was weak on the afternoon and evening of the 27th, severe thunderstorms were still able to develop across the central South Plains. A dryline was again in place cutting from north to south around the Interstate 27/US Highway 87 corridor creating low level convergence. Strong heating along the dryline allowed a capping inversion to break late in the afternoon. With ample moisture in place at the lowest levels of the atmosphere, isolated storms were able to take advantage of a very unstable atmosphere. Isolated thunderstorms initially developed in and around the Lubbock (Lubbock County) vicinity and moved northeastward producing severe wind gusts along with hail up to ping pong ball size.
episodes.200687: An isolated severe storm developed near Rehobeth and produced quarter sized hail.
episodes.200730: An approaching front combined with the inland progressing east coast sea breeze over a moist and unstable airmass produced a few strong to pulse severe storms in the evening across interior SE GA.
episodes.200767: Strong to severe right-moving supercells would be focused along a stalled frontal boundary across Southeast New Mexico and the higher elevations of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.200768: Strong to severe right-moving supercells would be focused along a stalled frontal boundary across Southeast New Mexico and the higher elevations of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico during the afternoon and evening.
episodes.201043: A cool front moved through during the evening, producing showers and thunderstorms. One particular storm became severe and produced damaging winds.
episodes.201087: A thunderstorm developed in the lee of the Absaroka Mountains and become severe as it moved toward Meeteetse, where the public reported quarter size hail west of town.
episodes.201440: Showers and thunderstorms produced between 1 and 3 inches of rainfall across portions of the Ozarks which caused localized flooding.
episodes.201604: An upper level trough of low pressure aloft was situated over the Intermountain West on April 27th. East of this feature, a warm front lifted into western Nebraska and became the focal point for thunderstorm development during the late afternoon hours. Initial thunderstorms developed over western Garden County and tracked northeast into abundant low level moisture, strong low level shear and increased instability where they quickly became severe.  Hail up to 3 inches in diameter and eleven tornadoes occurred  with the severe storms which continued into the mid evening hours. Activity finally weakened over northern Cherry County by late evening. A couple of tornadoes were rated EF2 with winds estimated up to 132 MPH.
episodes.201826: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into portions of northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 26th, to the north of a front located near the Red River and with the approach of an upper level disturbance. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind.||Another round of thunderstorms developed across the region during the early morning of the 27th, as the front moved northward as a warm front. The strongest storms produced hail up to nickel size.
episodes.201889: As a shortwave slowly marched across the Mid-South, aided by diurnal instability a few strong to severe storms were able to grow and produce large hail and some wind damage and knock down trees and powerlines. Peak intensity of a storm occurred over Lafayette County where widespread damage occurred.
episodes.202136: From April 26 through 30, a moist and unstable weather pattern affected Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The episode began as deep tropical moisture moved into the region from the southeast, interacting with deep-layer troughs and supportive jet dynamics aloft. This synoptic setup led to daily rounds of scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms, especially during the afternoons across the interior and western portions of Puerto Rico.
episodes.202214: The approach of an upper trough over the Southern Plains on April 26th helped to reinforce a weak cold front southeast into Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, and Northeast Texas during the late afternoon through the evening hours. Warm and humid air south of the front contributed to enhanced instability, with large scale forcing and adequate wind shear resulting in the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms during the late afternoon across Southern McCurtain County Oklahoma, which eventually spread into portions of Southwest Arkansas. These storms primarily produced large hail across portions of Little River and Union Counties during the evening, with a report of localized flash flooding in El Dorado in Union County as the storms slowed and produced locally heavy rainfall of 1-2 inches over the city in a short period of time.
episodes.202310: Strong storms moved over the local waters during the late afternoon and early evening of April 26.
episodes.202339: An upper level low moved over SOCAL during the last week of April and allow for the development of a few thunderstorms and high elevation snow.
episodes.202709: A round of storms developed during the later afternoon across the northern areas and progressed across our eastern half. These storms produced damaging winds and hail.

Tornado touched down approximately 3 miles southwest of Bingham in far northern Garden County. This tornado quickly increased in size as it moved northeast, impacting utility poles and trees along Highway 2. Just to the east, the tornado impacted a farmstead and overturned a freight train, producing EF2 damage. The tornado continued to move slowly northeast for the next hour, primarily impacting open country in rural southwest Cherry County. The tornado ended shortly after 6 PM MST, 11 miles north-northeast of Ashby Nebraska.
